sq.ANSWER:
Dijkstra’s Algorithm is a shortest path algorithm developed by Edsger W. Dijkstra in 1956. It is a greedy algorithm used to find the shortest path from a starting vertex (source node) to all other vertices in a weighted graph, provided the edge weights are non-negative.

Dijkstra’s Algorithm is widely used because:

1️. Efficient Pathfinding: It efficiently finds the shortest path in terms of time or cost from one point to all others in a graph — essential in many optimization problems.

2️. Non-negative Edges: It works accurately in graphs with positive edge weights, which are common in real-world scenarios (distances, time, cost, etc.)

3️. Dynamic Decision Making: By updating the shortest known distance to each neighbor dynamically, it can adjust and optimize travel paths quickly.

4️. Greedy Nature: Since it always picks the closest vertex, it avoids unnecessary longer paths and ensures optimality.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: What is Dijkstra’s Algorithm and why is it used in graph applications?

sq.ANSWER:
The key steps are:

1️. Initialize:

  • Set the distance of the source vertex to 0, and all others to ∞ (infinity).
  • Mark all vertices as unvisited.

2️. Select Minimum Vertex:

  • Choose the unvisited vertex with the smallest tentative distance.

3️. Update Distances:

  • For each unvisited neighbor of the current vertex, calculate the tentative distance from the source.
  • If this new distance is less than the current stored distance, update it.

4️. Mark as Visited:

  • After updating, mark the current vertex as visited.

5️. Repeat:

  • Repeat steps 2–4 until all vertices are visited.

6️. Result:

  • Display the shortest distance from the source to all other vertices.

lq.ANSWER:
C Program

#include <stdio.h>

#define INFINITY 9999

#define MAX 6

void dijkstra(int G[MAX][MAX], int n, int startnode) {

    int cost[MAX][MAX], distance[MAX], pred[MAX];

    int visited[MAX], count, mindistance, nextnode, i, j;

    // Create cost matrix

    for (i = 0; i < n; i++)

        for (j = 0; j < n; j++)

            if (G[i][j] == 0)

                cost[i][j] = INFINITY;

            else

                cost[i][j] = G[i][j];

    // Initialize distances and predecessors

    for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {

        distance[i] = cost[startnode][i];

        pred[i] = startnode;

        visited[i] = 0;

    }

    distance[startnode] = 0;

    visited[startnode] = 1;

    count = 1;

    // Find shortest path for all nodes

    while (count < n - 1) {

        mindistance = INFINITY;

        // Next node selection

        for (i = 0; i < n; i++)

            if (distance[i] < mindistance && !visited[i]) {

                mindistance = distance[i];

                nextnode = i;

            }

        visited[nextnode] = 1;

        // Update distances

        for (i = 0; i < n; i++)

            if (!visited[i])

                if (mindistance + cost[nextnode][i] < distance[i]) {

                    distance[i] = mindistance + cost[nextnode][i];

                    pred[i] = nextnode;

                }

 

        count++;

    }

    // Display results

    for (i = 0; i < n; i++)

        if (i != startnode) {

            printf("\nShortest distance from %c to %c: %d", startnode + 'A', i + 'A', distance[i]);

            printf("\nPath: %c", i + 'A');

            j = i;

            do {

                j = pred[j];

                printf(" <- %c", j + 'A');

            } while (j != startnode);

            printf("\n");

        }

}

int main() {

    int G[MAX][MAX] = {

        {0, 0, 2, 10, 0, 0},

        {0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 0},

        {2, 0, 0, 1, 0, 18},

        {10, 2, 1, 0, 11, 6},

        {0, 1, 0, 11, 0, 2},

        {0, 0, 18, 6, 2, 0}

    };

    dijkstra(G, MAX, 0); // Start from node A (index 0)

    return 0;

}
